name: Bingöl
summary_text: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): conservative east. Scored relative to the national score (0.15) for Turkey. Dossier finding: no sub-national divergence documented for this province — it is among the 73 units left at the national score (no province-specific ordinance, incident series or different legal system found). The dossier's only regional-grade note for the east is security practice (emergency-era policing, high police presence) rather than law. National context for its sources: a leaked omnibus package (the "11th Judicial Package", Oct 2025) would criminalise LGBT identity and advocacy (up to 3 years; same-sex ceremonies up to 4 years) and raise gender-affirming-care eligibility to 25 with a permanent-infertility mandate; the 2025 national monitoring report records hostility institutionalised as state policy.

sources.title: Türkiye: Draft Law Threatens LGBT People with Prison | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (29 Oct 2025): the leaked '11th Judicial Package' omnibus reform would amend the penal code to criminalise LGBT conduct and advocacy (up to 3 years for behaviour 'contrary to biological sex and general morality', up to 4 years for same-sex ceremonies) and the civil code to raise gender-affirming-care eligibility from 18 to 25 with a permanent-infertility mandate, exposing providers to fines and up to 7 years and patients to up to 3 years; 15 LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association objected. National context for this province.

Kaos GL LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025 (24 Feb 2026), 'A Major Siege': in 2025 hostility became explicit state policy (presidency-centred, with the family ministry implementing); documents 6 right-to-life violations (3 hate-motivated killings, trans people most affected), 89 torture/ill-treatment violations (up from 51), and 313 liberty violations (about 2.5x the prior year), based on media cases because the state keeps no hate-crime statistics. National context for this province.

sources.title: İstanbul police detain trans women for ID checks amid profiling concerns
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (only a site shell was returned); the underlying report covers about 20 trans women detained for identity checks in the Beyoglu district of Istanbul on 31 July 2025 (names recorded, videos filmed, no official reason given). Used here as national profiling context, not province-specific evidence.
